federal_ministry.name: Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy

how_to_address_head.head_title: Honourable Minister, Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy
how_to_address_head.through_title: Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy

regulators_and_core_agencies.name: Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC)
mandate: Consumer protection and quality of service enforcement

how_to_address_head.head_title: Executive Vice Chairman/Chief Executive Officer, Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC)

consumer_redress_channels: Complain to service provider first and obtain ticket/reference
If unresolved, call NCC toll-free 622 or use NCC consumer portal/email channels
regulators_and_core_agencies.authoritative_license_registry_hint: NCC ‘List of Licensees’ page (class and individual licensees)

regulators_and_core_agencies.name: National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA)
regulators_and_core_agencies.type: ICT/Digital Policy & Programs (regulatory overlap on IT/digital matters)

how_to_address_head.head_title: Director-General, National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA)

other_licensees.note: Nigeria has many class/individual licensees (ISPs, infra companies, VAS, MVNOs, etc.). Pull the full current list from the NCC license registry.

complaint_and_escalation_flow.step_1: Complain to the telecom operator first; obtain a ticket/reference number.
complaint_and_escalation_flow.step_2: If unresolved within the operator’s timeline, escalate to NCC using toll-free 622, NCC consumer email/portal, and attach ticket/reference and evidence.
complaint_and_escalation_flow.step_3: If fraud/crime is involved (SIM swap fraud, extortion), report to NPF and copy NCC.

evidence_checklist: Bank statement if charged via bank/card
